subject: 04_Advanced_Software_Eng
topic: Lecture 01: Foundations, Patriot Failure, Brooks & Ethics
instructor: Asst. Prof. Dr. Ali Fahim Ni'ma

questions.question: During continuous operation of a real-time defense tracking battery, an integer tenth-of-a-second clock counter is multiplied by a 24-bit fixed-point approximation of 1/10. Over 100 hours, what kinematic consequence directly caused the Dhahran Patriot missile failure?

options.A: The radar transmitter burned out due to CPU clock overclocking.
options.B: A 0.34-second clock drift shifted the radar range gate by ~687 meters, causing the system to track empty airspace.
options.C: The tracking software suffered a stack overflow when converting to 48-bit double precision.
options.D: The missile guidance fin locked up due to an integer division-by-zero exception.

questions.explanation: Truncating 1/10 at bit 24 introduced a negative drift of ~0.000000095s per tick. Over 100 hours (3.6M ticks), the clock lost 0.3433 seconds. At Mach 5 (1,676 m/s), the range gate shifted by ~687 meters, causing the radar to look where the Scud used to be.

questions.question: In his seminal paper 'No Silver Bullet', Fred Brooks distinguishes between Essential and Accidental complexity. Which of the following is an ESSENTIAL complexity inherent to software systems?

options.A: Managing manual memory allocation and garbage collection in C/C++.
options.B: Slow compilation and linking times on developer workstations.
options.C: Software having no physical geometric spatial representation (Invisibility).
options.D: Syntax verbosity in legacy assembly programming languages.

questions.explanation: Brooks identifies four inherent properties of essential complexity: Complexity, Conformity, Changeability, and Invisibility. Tooling, syntax, and compilation speed are accidental complexities.

questions.question: According to Brooks' Law formulated during the development of IBM OS/360, adding manpower to a late software project makes it later because:

options.A: Hardware memory limitations prevent additional developers from checking out code branches.
options.B: Onboarding creates training drag on existing experts, and inter-team communication channels grow quadratically (O(N^2)).
options.C: New developers invariably introduce syntax errors that break the automated compiler.
options.D: Operating system schedulers cannot handle multi-threaded development workflows.

questions.explanation: Brooks' Law demonstrates that communication overhead explodes as N(N-1)/2, while senior engineers lose productive time mentoring newcomers.

questions.question: In the formal IEEE 610.12 and Laprie/Avižienis dependability taxonomy, which sequence correctly models how software breakdowns emerge?

options.A: Human Error -> Static Fault/Defect in Artifact -> Runtime Internal Error State -> Observable Failure
options.B: Observable Failure -> Human Error -> Static Defect -> Bug

questions.explanation: A human cognitive mistake (Error) creates a static flaw (Fault/Defect) in code or documentation. When executed, it produces an invalid internal state (Error State), which manifests at the boundary as an observable Failure.

questions.question: Under Principle 1 (PUBLIC) of the ACM/IEEE Software Engineering Code of Ethics, what is a software engineer's primary professional obligation if pressured by management to ship software with known unverified safety risks?

options.A: Sign off immediately if the contract contains a legal liability disclaimer for the engineer.
options.B: Prioritize the commercial interests of the employer above all external considerations.
options.C: Refuse to approve compromised safety specifications and report the risk to appropriate authorities if unresolved.
options.D: Reduce the test suite coverage so that the CI/CD pipeline turns green before release.

questions.explanation: Principle 1 states that software engineers shall act consistently with the public interest, which supersedes employer loyalty when safety, health, or welfare is threatened.
